prose.title: The Long Haulers Got Paid to Take a Quarterback, Then Spent the Summer on Defense
prose.dek: Brian Cross took Jalen Hurts and {{f.team.0006.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of HammerTime's money for two future picks, put {{f.team.0006.idp_auction_share}} of his auction dollars into defenders, and opens year two {{f.team.0006.power_rank|ord}} in the preseason power rankings.

paragraphs: April found the Long Haulers top-heavy. Cross carried {{f.team.0006.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0006.cap_opening}} in salary, with {{f.team.0006.studs_opening}} real starters on offense: Jalen Hurts, a High-end QB1, Derrick Henry at running back, A.J. Brown at receiver, Tyler Warren, a High-end TE1, and Trevor Lawrence in the superflex. The {{f.team.0006.holes_opening}} holes were Jordan Mason at the second running back spot, Josh Downs at the second receiver spot, and Tre Tucker and Woody Marks in the two flexes, all replacement-level.

He did his shopping before the draft and paid in picks, not salary. In April his 2027 first- and second-round picks went to HammerTime for Hurts, and HammerTime added {{f.team.0006.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money to the deal, so Cross was paid to take on a {{f.team.0006.trade1_salary_in}} quarterback. In May a 2027 third bought Quentin Johnston and his {{f.team.0006.trade2_salary_in}} salary from Pure Greatness, and five later-round rookie picks went to Sex Manther for 3.04 and 3.06. Before the draft he took on {{f.team.0006.trade_salary_in_s1}} of salary in trades and sent none away.

There were no cuts and no extensions in that stretch. Two rookie deals ran out: Devon Witherspoon is still on the roster, and Will Levis went to the Expired Rookie Auction, where Cross bought him back.

t.0006.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: On draft day he flipped 2.03 and the 3.06 he had just bought to Gride for 2.05 and 2.10, then made {{f.team.0006.rookie_picks_count}} picks: Fernando Mendoza at 1.03, a slot that has produced a usable player more often than not, then Malachi Fields, Germie Bernard, Mike Washington Jr., Carson Beck at 3.04, Kevin Coleman and Keldric Faulk. Mendoza and Beck make two rookie quarterbacks behind Hurts and Lawrence. None of the class grades as a starter yet, which at this stage is the expectation, not a verdict.

At the Expired Rookie Auction he bought Tyjae Spears for {{f.team.0006.era_16165_price}} and Levis back for {{f.team.0006.era_16149_price}}. He tagged nobody. His cuts before the lock were small: six taxi-squad and minimum-salary bodies at no cost, and one real release, Theo Johnson in July, with {{f.team.0006.cut_16649_salary}} of salary and a {{f.team.0006.cut_16649_penalty}} penalty. A July trade with L.A. Looks sent Isaiah Bond and a 2027 fourth for safety Jordan Battle, Adonai Mitchell and a 2027 fifth, and on the day the auction roster locked he extended Hurts at {{f.team.0006.contract_14783_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0006.contract_14783_tcv}} in all.

t.0006.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: Then Cross spent the Free Agent Auction on defense. Of his {{f.team.0006.faa_spend}}, {{f.team.0006.idp_auction_spend}} went to defenders: Maxx Crosby for {{f.team.0006.faa_14225_price}} and Brian Burns for {{f.team.0006.faa_14171_price}}, both Elite DL1s, and Jordyn Brooks, an Elite LB1, for {{f.team.0006.faa_14892_price}}. It is a real defense, and like every defense in this league it is a footnote to the offense.

On offense he spent {{f.team.0006.faa_off_spend}}, and that is why the league table flatters him. It ranks value gained per dollar, and so little money that moved the lineup at all ranks high: {{f.team.0006.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}. The What it bought column is the honest one. Three depth players, George Holani, Jalen Nailor and Nick Mullens, and in total value added he was {{f.team.0006.faa_off_gain_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}.

The contract work ran through the auction. The lock-day restructure cut Hurts to {{f.team.0006.contract_14783_salary_2}} for 2026 without touching his {{f.team.0006.contract_14783_tcv_2}} total, a little room opened for bidding. {{f.team.0006.myac_faa}} auction buys and both Expired Rookie Auction buys got multi-year contracts, and so did two trade pickups, Jordan Battle and Gunnar Helm. One of those did not last: Levis, bought back and signed on, was cut in August with a {{f.team.0006.cut_16149_penalty}} penalty that lands on the 2027 cap. Josh Downs was extended in September at {{f.team.0006.contract_16187_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0006.contract_16187_tcv}} in all.

After the auction came the churn: {{f.team.0006.pickups_s3}} pickups before week one, most of them tight ends passing through. Zach Ertz, Darren Waller and Matthew Hibner all came and went, Helm arrived by trade, and Najee Harris and Malik Davis joined at running back. The {{f.team.0006.cuts_s3}} releases in that stretch cost {{f.team.0006.cuts_s3_penalty}} in penalties, all of it charged to 2027.

The lineup it built has the shape it had in April: {{f.team.0006.studs_today}} real starters in Hurts, Henry, Brown, Warren and Lawrence, and {{f.team.0006.holes_today}} holes, now George Holani at the second running back spot, Quentin Johnston at the second receiver spot, and Jordan Mason and Josh Downs in the flexes. The kicker, Jason Myers, led all kickers in points per game last year and cost {{f.team.0006.faa_12437_price}}.

paragraphs: Cross is a short story so far. The league's documented record starts him in {{f.team.0006.hist_first_season}}, and his one completed season produced a {{f.team.0006.hist_allplay_pct}} all-play record and no playoff trip. No titles, no division crowns, nothing on the wall yet, which is the easiest kind of history to improve on.

Outlast PG Time is the division that holds the last two champions, and Cross plays each of them five times: Pure Greatness won in {{f.league.title_years_0004}} and HammerTime in {{f.league.title_years_0005}}. The simulation likes them again, Pure Greatness {{f.league.power_rank_0004|ord}} with {{f.league.p_title_0004}} title odds and HammerTime {{f.league.power_rank_0005|ord}}. It puts the Long Haulers {{f.team.0006.power_rank|ord}}, with {{f.team.0006.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and a {{f.team.0006.sim_p_division}} chance at the division.

The next three years, filed the way Cross would file them. 2027: no first-round pick, because HammerTime owns it, and he congratulates HammerTime by name when they use it. The defense he bought this summer is still under contract and still the best thing on the depth chart. 2028: Mendoza or Beck takes the superflex from Lawrence, the Team finally fills the second receiver spot, and it is Let's GO season in the group chat. 2029, and this is a prediction, not a verdict: the Fantasy Gods square the account, and a Championship, capital C, ships to the Long Haulers.

Week one has barely started, with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done. Myers kicked two field goals, A.J. Brown caught three passes, and the Long Haulers have {{f.team.0006.wk_points_final}} points in the bank.
